title: Blood Tests Are Starting to Replace Brain Scans for Diagnosing Alzheimer's
hook: New blood-based biomarker tests are giving doctors a faster, more detailed way to diagnose Alzheimer's — without a brain scan, spinal tap, or a specialist's yearlong wait list.
key_points: Blood-based biomarker tests are increasingly replacing traditional Alzheimer's diagnostics like brain scans, spinal taps, and specialist cognitive assessments.
Traditional methods are burdensome and bottlenecked by specialist capacity — neurologist wait times can stretch for months or over a year.
The new blood tests give more nuanced results than a simple yes/no diagnosis, providing clinicians with more detailed information.
Because new Alzheimer's treatments work best when started early, researchers are studying how to bring these tests into primary care, where most patients are seen first.
The Alzheimer's Association has issued guidelines to help doctors start implementing blood-based tests in practice.
content_html: Diagnosing Alzheimer's has traditionally meant a brain scan, a spinal tap, or a long wait for a neurologist's cognitive assessment. A new generation of blood tests is starting to change that.
extra_html: Presented at the Alzheimer's Association International Conference, research on blood-based biomarker tests shows they can sidestep the most burdensome parts of traditional Alzheimer's diagnosis, which is bottlenecked by specialist capacity — neurologist wait times can stretch for months or, in some places, over a year. Rather than a simple yes/no diagnosis, the blood tests give clinicians more nuanced results, providing useful detail beyond just whether Alzheimer's is present. Because newer Alzheimer's treatments work best when started early, researchers are specifically studying how to bring these tests into primary care, where most patients are seen well before they ever reach a specialist. The Alzheimer's Association has already issued guidelines to help doctors start using blood-based tests in everyday practice.
